text: Looking into the `Interval.fromISO` / `Settings.throwOnInvalid` bug in src/interval.js now. ETA ~10 min.

`parseDigits` returns the number `NaN` when the input contains no parseable digits (e.g. `parseDigits("abc")`, `parseDigits("")`).

Trace (src/impl/digits.js:50-72): `parseInt(str, 10)` is `NaN`, so the fallback branch sets `value = ""`, the loop matches nothing (no hanidec char, no char code in any `numberingSystemsUTF16` range), and it returns `parseInt("", 10)` → `NaN`. There is no docstring stating a different return value.
Got it — investigating the `src/impl/util.js` bug (DateTime#plus across the 100 barrier through February). ETA ~15 min.

`match(input, regex, handlers)` (src/impl/tokenParser.js:247-267) returns a 2-element array `[rawMatches, matches]`:

- Input does NOT match: `input.match(regex)` is `null`, so it returns `[null, {}]` — raw matches `null`, and an **empty but truthy object** `{}` for the token map.
- Input matches: returns `[matches, all]`, where `matches` is the raw `String.prototype.match` array and `all` is `{ tokenChar: deserializedValue }`.

Its only caller is `explainFromTokens` (line 390), which does `[result, zone] = matches ? dateTimeFromMatches(matches) : [null, null]`. Because the failure branch yields `{}` (truthy), that ternary never takes the `[null, null]` path on failure: `dateTimeFromMatches({})` runs and returns `[{}, null]`, so `result` is `{}` rather than `null`.

`hasInvalidWeekData` (src/impl/conversions.js:100-112) returns an **`Invalid` object**, not `true`, when `obj.weekYear` is not an integer.

Trace: `validYear = isInteger(obj.weekYear)` (util.js:23-25 → `typeof o === "number" && o % 1 === 0`) is `false` for `2017.5`, `NaN`, `"2017"`, `undefined`, etc. Then line 105 `if (!validYear)` → line 106 returns `unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)`, i.e. `new Invalid("unit out of range", "you specified 2017.5 (of type number) as a weekYear, which is invalid")`.

For contrast, with a valid integer `weekYear` it returns `false` when everything is in range, otherwise an `Invalid` for the offending unit (weekNumber out of `1..weeksInWeekYear(weekYear)`, or weekday out of `1..7`). Callers (datetime.js:686-695) only test truthiness, so the `Invalid` object is what marks the data invalid.
Noted — investigating the src/datetime.js bug for `DateTime#isInDST()` in the 1974 US DST period. ETA ~20 min (after #1 and #4).

`Settings.defaultZone` (src/settings.js:61-63) is a **getter only**: `return defaultZone || LocalZone.instance;`. So when the internal `defaultZone` variable is `null`, it returns `LocalZone.instance` (the lazily-created singleton in src/zones/localZone.js), not `null` and not a "SystemZone".

Related details: there is no setter for `defaultZone` (assigning to it throws a TypeError); the supported API is `Settings.defaultZoneName`, whose setter stores `defaultZone = null` for any falsy input, and the getter then falls back to `LocalZone.instance` at read time.

If the `eval` throws, the `try/catch` in `run` (site/demo/demo.js:7-27) catches it, calls `console.error(e)` and returns the literal string `"[error]"` — the exception does not propagate and no error object is returned.

On success it returns: `"Invalid"` if `result.isValid === false`; `"[ DateTime " + result.toISO() + " ]"` for a DateTime; `"[ Duration " + JSON.stringify(result.toObject()) + " ]"` for a Duration; otherwise `JSON.stringify(result)`. (Note the try/catch only covers the `eval` line, so a value like `null` would throw later in the switch.)

After all `example(...)` calls, `demo` joins the accumulated strings with `""` and injects them into the DOM — it doesn't return them (the function returns `undefined`). site/demo/demo.js:80-87: it builds `all = "

Some Luxon examples

" + "

This is not meant to be a comprehensive showcase...

" + "" + examples.join("") + "
"`, then does `document.body.innerHTML = all`, replacing the page body with the table of examples. Each `example(code)` call (lines 28-36) pushes one complete `CODE//=> RESULT` string, where RESULT is `run(code)`.

`digitRegex({ numberingSystem }, append = "")` (src/impl/digits.js:74-76) falls back to `"latn"` when `numberingSystem` is not provided: `new RegExp(`${numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]}${append}`)`. So the default numbering system is `latn`, whose pattern is `\\d` (i.e. ASCII digits 0-9).

The `Settings.defaultZoneName` setter (src/settings.js:49-55) checks `if (!z)`: for any falsy value (empty string, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `false`) it sets the internal `defaultZone = null`; otherwise it sets `defaultZone = normalizeZone(z)`. So passing `""` clears the internal zone, and the `defaultZone` getter then falls back to `LocalZone.instance` (`defaultZone || LocalZone.instance`).
Noted — investigating the second src/impl/util.js bug (negative-year padding in toISODate). ETA ~22 min, after the urgent #11 and #1/#4.

Fixed. Root cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded the whole string (`("0".repeat(n) + input).slice(-n)`), so for negative years the sign fell inside the padding window (`-1` → `"00-1"`). It now pads the magnitude and re-attaches the sign: `-1` → `"-0001-01-01"`, `-44` → `"-0044-01-01"`, `-123` → `"-0123-01-01"`, while `1` → `"0001-01-01"` and `999` → `"0999-01-01"` are unchanged. Verified with the datetime suite and the full suite: 892 passed, only the 2 pre-existing container-ICU toFormat failures remain.

When `matches.Z` is defined (format had `Z`/`ZZ`/`ZZZ`), `dateTimeFromMatches` (src/impl/tokenParser.js:302-309) sets the zone to `new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` — a `FixedOffsetZone` whose `.fixed` is the parsed offset in minutes (e.g. `330` for `+05:30`), produced earlier by the `offset(...)` deserializer via `signedOffset(h, m)`. Note it uses the constructor directly, not `FixedOffsetZone.instance(...)`.

The function returns the array `[vals, zone]`, where `vals` is the field-name→number object (line 327-334; `Z` itself is dropped since `toField("Z")` is `null`). For contrast: if `matches.z` is set instead, zone is `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`; if neither, `zone = null`.

Noted — investigating the src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js bug (invalid zone / non-numeric offset should make the zone and any DateTime using it invalid). ETA ~25 min, queued behind the urgent #11 and #1/#4/#8.

Fixed. `Interval.fromISO` (src/interval.js:134-170) now wraps each `DateTime.fromISO` call in its own try/catch, so a throw under `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is treated as "not a valid DateTime" and the `Duration.fromISO` fallback still runs. With `throwOnInvalid = true`: `"2016-01-01/P1Y"`, `"P1Y/2016-01-01"`, `"2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M"` all parse valid; `"hello"`, `""`, `null`, `"foo/bar"`, and `"2016-01-01/2015-01-01"` still throw. Behavior with `throwOnInvalid = false` is unchanged. Also fixed the message typo `asISO 8601` → `as ISO 8601` (no test asserts that string). Verified: test/interval 127/127 pass; full suite 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing container-ICU toFormat failures.

In `hasInvalidTimeData` (src/impl/conversions.js:139-157), hour 24 is valid only through the second disjunct of `validHour` (line 143):

```js
const validHour =
  integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) ||
  (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0);
```

So `hour === 24` is accepted only when `minute`, `second` and `millisecond` are all strictly `0` (the first disjunct rejects 24 since it's > 23). If any of them is non-zero (or missing), `validHour` is false and the function returns `unitOutOfRange("hour", hour)` — an `Invalid` object blaming the hour.

Overall it returns `false` when the time data is valid, otherwise an `Invalid` object for the first failing unit in the order hour → minute → second → millisecond.
Per the JSDoc on `Zone#formatOffset(ts, format)` (src/zone.js:48-58), the `format` argument accepts `'narrow'`, `'short'`, or `'techie'`, returning `'+6'`, `'+06:00'`, or `'+0600'` respectively.

Fixed. Root cause: the conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing three entries — `casualMatrix.years.quarters`, `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds`, and `accurateMatrix.years.quarters` — so `convert()` produced `NaN` (surfacing as `0`), e.g. `Duration.fromObject({years:1}).normalize().as('quarters')` returned 0 instead of 4. Added `quarters: 4` to both `years` maps and `seconds: 91*24*60*60` to the casual `quarters` map. Verified: all 81 unit pairs × both accuracies now convert consistently (days→hours=24, years→quarters=4, quarters→seconds=7,862,400, etc.); test/duration 114/114 pass; full suite 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing container-ICU toFormat failures.
